items.reasoning: PrivateLink consumer interface endpoint connects privately to the SaaS provider endpoint service, with security groups limiting clients. No inbound access to company resources is exposed.

wrongOptions.A: Correct; consumer-side interface endpoint and endpoint security group.
wrongOptions.B: VPN requires tunnel management and does not provide the narrowly scoped SaaS endpoint pattern.
wrongOptions.C: Peering creates broad routed network connectivity and requires coordination.
wrongOptions.D: Reverses provider and consumer roles and exposes a company-provided service.

items.memoryTip: SaaS private API + no inbound exposure = consumer PrivateLink endpoint.

wrongOptions.D: PrivateLink publishes individual services, not general-purpose internet egress.

items.reasoning: The source selects D, but aws:SourceIp means the IP address making the EC2 API request, not the CIDR source inside the security-group ingress rule. No option fully meets the preventive requirement.

wrongOptions.A: EventBridge/Lambda can remediate a rule after it is created, but does not prevent the creation operation.
wrongOptions.B: Config's authorized-ports rule evaluates configuration, not a preventive deny of any 0.0.0.0/0 rule.
wrongOptions.C: Allow-based SCP using aws:SourceIp does not inspect security group ingress CIDR; also SCP Allow is not a targeted guardrail.
wrongOptions.D: Deny-based SCP using aws:SourceIp tests API caller source address, not requested ingress CIDR.

items.memoryTip: aws:SourceIp = API caller IP, NOT security-group ingress CIDR.
